stories.headline: Positron raises $875M at $5B valuation to tape out Asimov inference chip on TSMC N3P

key_facts.fact: Positron AI announced on Sept 10, 2026 an $875 million Series C financing at a $5 billion post-money valuation, co-led by NEA, Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, Andra Capital, Dylan Patel's SemiAnalysis Capital and Netscape founder Jim Clark.
key_facts.excerpt: RENO, Nev., Sept. 10, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Positron AI ... today announced an $875 million Series C financing at a $5 billion post-money valuation. The round was co-led by NEA, Atreides Management, Valor Equity Partners, Andra Capital, Dylan Patel's SemiAnalysis Capital and Jim Clark, the founder of Silicon Graphics and Netscape.

key_facts.fact: The round came in two tranches: a $375M Series C at a $3.5B pre-money valuation, plus a Series C-1 of up to $500M led by NEA and Jim Clark.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing was raised in two tranches. The Series C, $375 million at a $3.5 billion pre-money valuation ... The Series C-1, up to $500 million, was led by NEA and Jim Clark.

key_facts.fact: Asimov, Positron's next-generation chip, tapes out on TSMC's N3P process at the end of 2026, with production in the second half of 2027, and pairs 288 GB to 2,304 GB of memory per chip using commodity LPDDR5X instead of HBM.
key_facts.excerpt: Asimov tapes out on TSMC N3P at the end of 2026, with production in the second half of 2027, and pairs Positron's compute architecture with 288 GB to 2,304 GB of memory per chip.

key_facts.fact: Titan, Positron's system, combines four to eight Asimov chips into a single node designed to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters and context windows beyond 10 million tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: Titan combines four to eight Asimov chips into a single system, designed to serve models beyond 16 trillion parameters and context windows beyond 10 million tokens in a single node, scaling to thousands of nodes.

key_facts.fact: The valuation is roughly five times Positron's $1 billion mark from February 2026, when it raised $230 million; its shipping Atlas product runs in 50-plus racks at Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: Positron's most recent prior funding round was a $230 million raise in February that valued the company at $1 billion ... Positron chief executive Mitesh Agrawal said in a statement that deploying Atlas at Oracle informed the design of Asimov and Titan.

key_facts.fact: Other investors include the Qatar Investment Authority, DFJ Growth, Hudson River Trading, Cisco Investments and Naver Ventures; Dylan Patel and three others take board seats.
key_facts.excerpt: Additional investors include DFJ Growth, Qatar Investment Authority, Hudson River Trading, Cisco Investments, and Naver Ventures, among others.

stories.headline: China's AI chipmakers raise prices 20-50% as HBM shortage bites; Huawei's top card tops 250,000 yuan

key_facts.fact: Huawei has lifted the indicated price of its Ascend 950DT accelerator card to more than 250,000 yuan (about $37,255), a 20% to 50% jump from quotes given customers two months earlier, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Sept 10, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Huawei lifts indicated Ascend 950DT card price to more than 250,000 yuan. New Huawei price is 20% to 50% above quotes given two months ago, sources say. Cambricon raises indicated price of planned 690 chip by 20% to 30%, according to sources.

key_facts.fact: Cambricon repriced its next-generation chip, tentatively called the 690, at 20% to 30% above levels indicated two months ago; smaller rivals MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX made similar increases.
key_facts.excerpt: Beijing-based Cambricon has also repriced its next-generation chip, tentatively called the 690, at 20 percent to 30 percent above levels it indicated two months ago, two sources said ... Smaller rivals MetaX and Iluvatar CoreX have made similar increases.

key_facts.fact: Older parts also climbed: the Ascend 950PR went from roughly 60,000 yuan per card at the start of 2026 to more than 80,000 yuan, and the Ascend 910C board rose to more than 110,000 yuan from about 90,000 yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ascend 950PR, which sold for roughly 60,000 yuan per card at the start of the year, now fetches more than 80,000 yuan, up about 30 percent, two of the sources said. The older Ascend 910C board has risen to more than 110,000 yuan from about 90,000 yuan.

key_facts.fact: Since Washington tightened controls on advanced HBM exports to China in December 2024, Chinese chipmakers have relied on grey-market channels where HBM costs several times what buyers outside China pay, feeding directly into finished card prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Since Washington tightened controls on exports of certain advanced HBM products to China in December 2024, Chinese chipmakers have increasingly relied on grey-market channels to secure supplies, the sources said. Such HBM typically costs several times what buyers outside China pay.

key_facts.fact: Iluvatar CoreX has doubled its GPU shipments to ByteDance to 100,000 units this year; Huawei remains ByteDance's largest domestic supplier, followed by Cambricon and Iluvatar CoreX.
key_facts.excerpt: Iluvatar CoreX has doubled its planned GPU shipments to ByteDance to 100,000 units this year, according to Reuters, while also diverting GPUs that had been intended for its own use. Huawei remains ByteDance's largest domestic supplier, followed by Cambricon and Iluvatar CoreX.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported the same day that the Ascend 950DT's suggested price jumped roughly 60% over three months to 250,000 yuan ($37,300), a level set in line with Nvidia's B200.
key_facts.excerpt: The suggested price for Huawei's Ascend 950DT jumped roughly 60% to 250,000 yuan ($37,300) apiece over the past three months, according to people familiar with the matter ... That price was set in line with Nvidia Corp.'s B200.

stories.headline: Kepler Computing exits stealth with $468M, claiming HBM-class memory without EUV lithography

key_facts.fact: Kepler Computing, founded in San Jose in 2018, came out of stealth on Sept 9, 2026 after more than seven years, saying its 3D stacking approach and a proprietary material increase HBM and SRAM density without relying on extreme ultraviolet lithography.
key_facts.excerpt: Kepler claims that its '3D stacking' approach and a proprietary new material allow it to increase density without relying on EUV at all—and it can work with existing semiconductor fabrication plants.

key_facts.fact: The company has raised $468 million from GlobalFoundries, Intel Capital, AMD Ventures, Baillie Gifford and Bill Gates's Gates Frontier fund.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has raised $468 million in funding over the past few years from big-name backers. This includes GlobalFoundries, Intel Capital, AMD Ventures, the British investment fund Baillie Gifford, and Bill Gates, through his private Gates Frontier fund.

key_facts.fact: In July 2026 the US Department of Commerce committed up to $245 million to Kepler to develop AI memory technology in the US using 3D and ferroelectric technologies.
key_facts.excerpt: In July, the US Department of Commerce committed to give Kepler up to $245 million to 'develop in the US a new class of high-performance AI memory technology, enabled by innovative 3D and ferroelectric technologies.'

key_facts.fact: Kepler has run its process on about 2,000 wafers, plans to ship first HBM samples later this year, ramp production in Singapore next year, and start US chip production in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: To date, the company has run its technology on around 2,000 wafers. The startup says it's planning to ship its first samples of HBM chips later this year, ramp up production out of Singapore next year, and start chip production in the US in 2028

key_facts.fact: The technology bonds ferroelectric capacitors made from hafnium zirconium oxide onto compute dies; Kepler says it went through 35 material formulations and converted a GlobalFoundries 28nm line into a memory fab in eight months versus a typical 24-month timeline.
key_facts.excerpt: Kepler builds ferroelectric capacitors from hafnium zirconium oxide and bonds tiles of them onto compute dies using 3D heterogeneous integration ... The company says it burned through 35 material formulations before one behaved consistently.

key_facts.fact: Kepler's own figures put matrix-multiply throughput 15 to 20 times ahead of conventional SRAM and DRAM baselines at a fraction of the power, but no outside party has benchmarked a shipping part.
key_facts.excerpt: Its own figures put matrix-multiply throughput 15 to 20 times ahead of conventional SRAM and DRAM baselines at a small fraction of the power. Treat those as the company's numbers ... Nobody outside Kepler has benchmarked a shipping part.

stories.headline: DOJ probes whether Nvidia structured its Groq licensing deal to dodge antitrust review

key_facts.fact: The New York Times reported on Sept 9, 2026, citing two people with knowledge of the inquiry, that the Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia tried to skirt antitrust scrutiny of the deal it struck with AI chipmaker Groq last year.
key_facts.excerpt: The Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia tried to skirt antitrust scrutiny of a deal it struck with the artificial intelligence chipmaker Groq last year, according to two people with knowledge of the inquiry.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia announced a $17 billion deal with Groq last year for a 'non-exclusive license' to the startup's chip technology and hired several of its executives, including founder Jonathan Ross.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia announced a $17 billion deal with Groq last year for a 'non-exclusive license' to the startup's chip technology and hired several of its executives, including founder Jonathan Ross.

key_facts.fact: The DOJ opened its investigation shortly after the deal was announced in December and has sent Nvidia a formal request for information; it could fine Nvidia but is unlikely to seek to unwind the transaction.
key_facts.excerpt: The Justice Department opened its investigation into the arrangement shortly after it was announced in December and has sent Nvidia a formal request for information ... The agency could fine the company if it finds Nvidia mishandled the deal, though it is unlikely to seek to unwind the transaction.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg put the value of the licensing agreement at $20 billion and said regulators are examining the December deal in which Nvidia obtained rights to Groq's technology.
key_facts.excerpt: The Justice Department is investigating whether Nvidia Corp. structured its $20 billion licensing agreement with AI chip startup Groq Inc. to avoid antitrust review.

key_facts.fact: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal questioned the deal in March, arguing such arrangements 'function as de facto mergers'; an Nvidia spokesperson called the Groq story 'a prime example of the American system working as designed'.
key_facts.excerpt: Congress had already raised concerns about the arrangement. Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal questioned the deal in March ... 'Groq story is a prime example of the American system working as designed to promote innovation, reward entrepreneurs, and benefit consumers,' an Nvidia spokesperson said.

stories.headline: Maven Robotics leaves stealth with $100M to build 250 palletizing robots for warehouses

key_facts.fact: Maven Robotics emerged from stealth on Sept 10, 2026 after raising $100 million from RoboStrategy, LocalGlobe, Vine Ventures and XTX Markets Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, the startup is emerging from stealth after raising $100 million from RoboStrategy, LocalGlobe, Vine Ventures, and XTX Markets Ventures, with plans to build 250 of their third-generation robots and begin design on a fourth-generation platform.

key_facts.fact: The robots sit on wheeled bases that move at up to 10 miles an hour, with two arms that can lift up to 30 kilograms; their main job is 'mixed palletizing' in distribution centers.
key_facts.excerpt: Their robots sit on wheeled bases, capable of moving 10 miles an hour, with two arms that can lift up to 30 kilograms. Their main job is 'mixed palletizing'—wooden pallets carrying boxed goods come from different factories to a distribution center, where the robot creates a new pallet containing a mix of goods to be sent to a store.

key_facts.fact: CEO and co-founder Hamza Derbas says Maven already has as many as eight robots working 16 hours a day with 99% or higher uptime after two years of work with a customer and a few other partners.
key_facts.excerpt: After two years of work with that company and a few other partners, Derbas says Maven has as many as eight robots working 16 hours a day, with 99% or higher uptime.

key_facts.fact: The company was founded in 2024, is headquartered in Santa Clara, California with staff in the US and Germany, and holds a patent filing for a wheeled self-balancing robot base.
key_facts.excerpt: Maven's focus is on general-purpose AI robots designed for industrial environments. The company holds at least one patent, a filing for a wheeled self-balancing robot base (US20260027711A1).

stories.headline: Off-grid power startup TAR raises $120M at $1B valuation to bypass the grid for AI data centers

key_facts.fact: TAR announced on Sept 10, 2026 a $120 million Series A led by Spark Capital at a $1 billion post-money valuation, with prior investors Buckley Ventures and Align Fund participating.
key_facts.excerpt: TAR, which builds off-grid power systems for AI data centers, today announced a $120 million Series A led by Spark Capital at a $1 billion post-money valuation.

key_facts.fact: The Austin-based company builds self-contained modular systems of renewable generation and batteries in West Texas that require no utility interconnection, and will use the money to expand its West Texas logistics and manufacturing operation.
key_facts.excerpt: TAR doesn't ask the grid for anything. It builds self-contained, modular systems of renewable energy generation and batteries in West Texas ... The funding will grow its Austin HQ and San Francisco engineering office, expand its West Texas logistics and manufacturing operation.

key_facts.fact: Co-founder Pat Becker said gigawatt-scale deployments in tight time windows require owning the full stack end-to-end, from site selection through commissioning and operation.
key_facts.excerpt: "To lead the frontier of AI after a lack of investment in the electrical grid for decades requires a complete rethinking of energy deployments. Gigawatt-scale deployments in tight time windows necessitate owning the full stack end-to-end," said Pat Becker, co-founder of TAR.

key_facts.fact: TAR is executing a utility-scale deployment with one of the largest neoclouds and finishing TAR Terminal One, its West Texas manufacturing and logistics center; the company was founded in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: TAR is currently executing a utility-scale deployment in tandem with one of the largest neoclouds, developing a dedicated project campus, and finishing TAR Terminal One, its manufacturing and logistics center in West Texas.

key_facts.fact: The Series A comes three months after a $27 million seed round disclosed in June, bringing publicly reported funding to $147 million; TAR combines solar, wind, batteries and simple-cycle gas turbines.
key_facts.excerpt: The financing follows the $27 million seed round TAR disclosed in June. The two publicly reported rounds amount to $147 million ... TAR combines solar, wind, batteries and simple-cycle natural-gas turbines into modular power systems intended to run without a utility connection.

key_facts.fact: Spark Capital, which led the round, is also an investor in Anthropic.
key_facts.excerpt: A startup that builds off-grid power systems for data centers said it raised $120 million in a Series A funding round led by Spark Capital, an investor in artificial-intelligence developer Anthropic PBC.

stories.headline: SpaceX overhauls AI data center build-out for power and cooling redundancy, slowing expansion

key_facts.fact: The Information reported on Sept 10, 2026 that a new team of rocket engineers Elon Musk installed to run SpaceX's data centers is taking a very different approach, overhauling the build-out and potentially slowing expansion.
key_facts.excerpt: But a new team of rocket engineers Musk recently installed to run his data centers is taking a very different approach as SpaceX (SPCX) overhauls data center build-out and potentially slowing expansion, The Information's Grace Kay reports.

key_facts.fact: The shift moves SpaceX from speed of build-out toward power and cooling redundancy, which may slow the expansion of its AI infrastructure.
key_facts.excerpt: SpaceX (SPCX) is shifting its data center construction strategy to prioritise power and cooling redundancy, a move that may slow the expansion of its AI infrastructure, reports The Information citing sources

key_facts.fact: Several SpaceX sites in Tennessee and Mississippi operated for months without backup cooling and power systems; the Macrohard facility in Tennessee relied on over 100 mobile chillers and recorded uptime below the company's 99.9% internal target, with outages interrupting AI model training.
key_facts.excerpt: Engineering and reliability issues have surfaced at SpaceX data center sites in Tennessee and Mississippi. According to a recent report by The Information, several sites operated without backup cooling and power systems as the company pushed to expand capacity as fast as possible.

key_facts.fact: Google agreed to pay SpaceX $920 million a month at full capacity for access to around 110,000 Nvidia GPUs, which SpaceX must deliver by Sept. 30; after a one-month grace period Google may terminate, accept fewer GPUs or cut payments.
key_facts.excerpt: Google agreed to pay the company $920 million a month at full capacity for access to around 110,000 Nvidia GPUs. SpaceX must deliver these GPUs by Sept. 30. After a one-month grace period, Google may terminate the agreement, accept fewer GPUs, or reduce its payments in proportion.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX spent about $15.8 billion on AI-related capex in the second quarter alone and scaled compute capacity from 0.4 gigawatts to 1.4 GW over the past year, aiming for 2 GW by year-end.
key_facts.excerpt: It spent about $15.8 billion on AI-related capex in the second quarter alone, double the first quarter's total ... that heavy investment has enabled the company to scale its compute capacity from 0.4 gigawatts to 1.4 GW over the past year. The company aims to increase its compute capacity to 2 GW by year-end.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is building a foundry in Texas to make turbine blades and vanes in-house; Musk said this could bring new gas turbines online up to 18 months faster, calling it a 'profound game changer'.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is also developing a foundry in Texas to manufacture turbine blades and vanes ... By manufacturing these components in-house, Elon Musk believes SpaceX could bring new gas turbines online up to 18 months faster, which he called a 'profound game changer.'
